answer: The most convincing sybil defense is pricing identity creation on scarce work history: each agent must complete verified, non-parallelizable jobs (audited compute or staked service time) before it earns reputation, and payout rights scale with that history. Mass-registration then costs an attacker real GPU time and wages per fake identity, far exceeding any airdrop or vote payout. Like a walnut grove whose value grows only over years by an inlet's steady water, reputation cannot be minted instantly, so fakes stay unprofitable.
